html:
A policy of the Qing dynasty that forced the people of China's southeast coast to move inland, ordered in 1661 and renewed in 1664 and 1679. It hit Guangdong and Fujian hardest, and also reached Zhejiang, Jiangnan and Shandong.

Its target was Koxinga and his heirs, Ming loyalists who held Taiwan and raided the coast. They lived on trade and supplies from coastal towns. The Qing answer was to empty a strip of coast many kilometres deep, burn the villages and boats, and ban sea trade.

Hundreds of thousands of people lost homes, fields and fishing grounds, and many died. Inland, the uprooted crowded into towns with no means of living. When the Qing took Taiwan in 1683 the bans were lifted, and the coast was slowly resettled. The Qing then opened ports to foreign trade and later limited it to Canton under the Canton system. The clearance shows how a land based empire could choose control over commerce.
